Taxonomic Backbone Management Shiny App - Development Plan

Overview

App Name: shiny_app_taxo_backbone()

Purpose: Interactive Shiny application for managing the taxonomic backbone database, including: - Adding new taxonomic names to table_taxa - Updating existing taxonomic records - Setting and managing synonymy relationships - Canceling existing synonymy - Searching and browsing the taxonomic hierarchy

Target Users: Database administrators and taxonomists with write permissions on the taxa database

Core Architecture

1. Main App Structure

File: R/shiny_app_taxo_backbone.R

Following existing app patterns (shiny_app_query_plots.R, shiny_app_taxonomic_match.R):

shiny_app_taxo_backbone <- function(pool_taxa = NULL, language = "fr") {
  # Main app entry point
  # - Initialize translator (init_translator())
  # - Create UI with conditional authentication panel
  # - Server with database connection management
  # - Session cleanup on exit
}

Key components: - Database authentication using mod_database_login_ui/server - Connection to taxa database only (stored in .db_env$pool_taxa) - Language toggle (EN/FR) with shiny.i18n - Modular architecture with separate modules for each function - Session cleanup with cleanup_connections() and q("no")

Module Architecture

Module 1: Taxa Search & Browser

File: R/mod_taxa_search.R

Purpose: Search and display taxonomic records

UI Components: - Search filters: - Genus/Species/Family/Order text inputs - ID search (idtax_n) - Exact match toggle - Synonymy filter (show/hide synonyms) - Results display: - DT datatable with taxonomic hierarchy - Columns: idtax_n, tax_gen, tax_esp, tax_fam, tax_order, tax_famclass, idtax_good_n (synonym), tax_rank, authors - Click to select record for editing - Statistics panel: - Total taxa count - Families/Genera/Species counts - Synonyms count

Server Functions: - mod_taxa_search_server(id, pool_taxa, i18n) - Returns: reactive selected taxon ID

Database queries: - Uses query_taxa() for searching - Direct tbl(pool_taxa, "table_taxa") for browsing

Module 2: Add New Taxa

File: R/mod_taxa_add.R

Purpose: Add new taxonomic entries using add_entry_taxa()

UI Components: - Step 1: Search Tropicos (optional) - Text input for species name - Button to search Tropicos API - Display Tropicos results (if found) - Select from results or manual entry

  • Step 2: Taxonomic Information
    • Required fields:
      • Genus (tax_gen)
      • Species epithet (tax_esp) - optional for genus-level
      • Family (tax_fam)
    • Auto-populated fields (if genus exists):
      • Order (tax_order)
      • Class (tax_famclass)
    • Optional fields:
      • Infraspecific rank (tax_rank1: var./subsp./f.)
      • Infraspecific name (tax_name1)
      • Authors (author1, author2, author3)
      • Year of description
      • Full name with authors (tax_tax)
    • Morphotaxa checkbox
    • Growth form selection (choose_growth_form())
  • Step 3: Synonymy (optional)
    • Checkbox: “This is a synonym”
    • Search for accepted name:
      • Genus/Species inputs
      • ID input
      • Display matches
    • Select accepted name
  • Step 4: Review & Submit
    • Summary of new entry
    • Validation warnings
    • Duplicate check display
    • Confirm button

Server Functions: - mod_taxa_add_server(id, pool_taxa, i18n) - Wraps add_entry_taxa() but with Shiny UI instead of console prompts - Returns: reactive notification of successful addition

Validations: - Check genus exists in database (warn if new) - Check family exists (warn if new) - Check for duplicates - Validate tax_tax matches genus/species - Validate taxonomic hierarchy consistency

Module 3: Update Existing Taxa

File: R/mod_taxa_update.R

Purpose: Update taxonomic records using update_dico_name()

UI Components: - Current Record Display (from Module 1 selection) - Read-only display of current values - Highlight synonym status

  • Update Form
    • All editable fields:
      • Genus, Species, Family, Order, Class
      • Infraspecific ranks and names
      • Authors
      • Introduced status
      • Tax ranks
    • Change tracking: highlight modified fields
  • Modification Actions:
    • Update button (applies changes)
    • Reset button (revert to original)
    • History button (show modification log via get_updates_diconame())

Server Functions: - mod_taxa_update_server(id, selected_taxon_id, pool_taxa, i18n) - Wraps update_dico_name() - Input: reactive taxon ID from search module - Returns: reactive success/failure status

Features: - Show backup records before modification - Confirmation dialog for changes - Display affected synonyms (if any point to this taxon) - Option to create backup (add_backup = TRUE)

Module 4: Synonymy Management

File: R/mod_taxa_synonymy.R

Purpose: Manage synonym relationships

UI Components: - Current Synonymy Display - If selected taxon is a synonym: show accepted name - If selected taxon has synonyms: list all synonyms - Synonym network visualization (optional)

  • Set Synonymy Panel
    • Search for accepted name:
      • Genus/Species/ID inputs
      • Display search results
    • Select accepted name
    • Confirm dialog with cascade warning (if taxon has synonyms)
    • Set button
  • Cancel Synonymy Panel
    • Current synonym status
    • Warning: “This will mark taxon as accepted”
    • Confirm button
    • Cancel synonymy action

Server Functions: - mod_taxa_synonymy_server(id, selected_taxon_id, pool_taxa, i18n) - Uses update_dico_name() with synonym_of or cancel_synonymy parameters - Returns: reactive status

Features: - Cascade handling: if taxon A → B, and B → C, warn about chain - Display all affected records - Validation: prevent circular synonymy

Module 5: Taxonomic Hierarchy Viewer

File: R/mod_taxa_hierarchy.R

Purpose: Visual display of taxonomic hierarchy

UI Components: - Interactive tree visualization (using visNetwork or collapsibleTree) - Breadcrumb navigation (Class → Order → Family → Genus → Species) - Statistics by rank: - Number of families per order - Number of genera per family - Number of species per genus - Export hierarchy to CSV/Excel

Server Functions: - mod_taxa_hierarchy_server(id, pool_taxa, i18n) - Queries table_taxa for hierarchy aggregation - Returns: NULL (display only)

navbarPage (after authentication)

Conditional UI States

  • Tabs 3 & 4 disabled when no taxon selected
  • Validation warnings displayed inline
  • Confirmation dialogs for destructive actions

Database Interaction

Required Database Access

Tables used: - table_taxa (main taxonomic table) - table_tax_famclass (class lookup) - table_traits_measures (for growth form data via add_sp_traits_measures()) - followup_updates_diconames (modification history)

Permissions needed: - READ: All users - WRITE: Only users with taxonomist role (verify on connect)

Connection Management

# In server function
if (is.null(pool_taxa)) {
  login_output <- mod_database_login_server("login")
  pool_reactive <- login_output$pool_taxa  # NOTE: taxa DB, not main DB!
  authenticated_reactive <- login_output$authenticated
} else {
  pool_reactive <- shiny::reactive(pool_taxa)
  authenticated_reactive <- shiny::reactive(TRUE)
  .db_env$pool_taxa <- pool_taxa
}

# Session cleanup
session$onSessionEnded(function() {
  tryCatch({
    cleanup_connections()
  }, error = function(e) {
    cli::cli_alert_warning("Failed to cleanup connections: {e$message}")
  })
  shiny::stopApp()
  q("no")
})

Function Adaptations

Adapting add_entry_taxa() for Shiny

Current function uses console prompts (readline(), choose_prompt()).

Shiny adaptation strategy: 1. Create wrapper function add_entry_taxa_shiny() that: - Takes all parameters explicitly (no interactive prompts) - Returns structured list with status, messages, new_id - Handles errors gracefully with tryCatch - Skips console output, returns data for Shiny display

  1. OR: Use existing function with parameters fully specified
    • All interactive sections bypassed by providing parameters
    • Set search_name_tps = "" to skip Tropicos in function
    • Do Tropicos search in Shiny module separately

Recommendation: Option 2 (use existing function) is cleaner, no duplication

Adapting update_dico_name() for Shiny

Current function uses: - choose_prompt() for confirmations - print() for displaying results

Shiny adaptation: - Set ask_before_update = FALSE (confirmation in Shiny UI) - Set show_results = FALSE (display in Shiny) - Capture return values and display in Shiny notifications

Development Workflow (per CLAUDE.md)

1. Create Feature Branch

git checkout -b feature/taxo-backbone-app

2. Development Steps

Phase 1: Core structure 1. Create R/shiny_app_taxo_backbone.R (main app) 2. Create R/mod_taxa_search.R (Module 1) 3. Add translations 4. Test basic search functionality

Phase 2: Add functionality 5. Create R/mod_taxa_add.R (Module 2) 6. Test adding taxa (read-only DB first!) 7. Create R/mod_taxa_update.R (Module 3) 8. Test updating taxa

Phase 3: Synonymy management 9. Create R/mod_taxa_synonymy.R (Module 4) 10. Test synonymy operations

Phase 4: Visualization & polish 11. Create R/mod_taxa_hierarchy.R (Module 5) 12. Add About page 13. UI/UX improvements

Phase 5: Documentation & testing 14. Document all functions with roxygen2 15. Update NEWS.md (ask user first!) 16. Integration testing 17. User testing with taxonomists

3. Before Each Commit

  • Run devtools::document()
  • Test app launch
  • Check translations load correctly

4. Commit Messages

Follow existing patterns:

feat: add taxonomic backbone management app structure
feat: add taxa search and browse module
feat: add new taxa creation module with Tropicos integration
feat: add taxa update and synonymy management
docs: add taxonomic backbone app documentation

5. Pull Request

  • Create PR to master
  • Request review from Gilles Dauby
  • Update NEWS.md after approval (ask user first!)

Testing Strategy

Unit Testing (if tests/ added)

  • Test search queries return expected results
  • Test validation logic (duplicates, hierarchy)
  • Test synonym cascade logic

Integration Testing

  1. Add taxa workflow:
    • Add new genus
    • Add species in that genus
    • Add variety
    • Set as synonym
  2. Update taxa workflow:
    • Update genus name (should affect species)
    • Update family (should warn)
  3. Synonymy workflow:
    • Set synonym
    • Check cascade (synonyms of synonyms)
    • Cancel synonymy
    • Verify table_idtax updates

User Acceptance Testing

  • Test with actual taxonomists
  • Verify Tropicos integration works
  • Check modification history tracking
  • Test with non-admin users (should fail gracefully)

Security Considerations

Database Permissions

  • Verify write permissions on connect
  • Graceful error if user lacks permissions
  • Display read-only mode warning

Input Validation

  • Sanitize all text inputs (SQL injection protection via parameterized queries)
  • Validate taxonomic names (no special characters except periods, hyphens)
  • Prevent circular synonymy
  • Check for orphaned records

Backup Strategy

  • Always use add_backup = TRUE for update_dico_name()
  • Log all modifications to followup_updates_diconames
  • Display modification history before destructive actions

Dependencies

R Packages (add to DESCRIPTION if missing)

  • shiny (already present)
  • shinyjs (already present)
  • shiny.i18n (already present)
  • DBI, RPostgres (already present)
  • pool (for connection pooling)
  • DT (datatables)
  • dplyr, tidyr (data manipulation)
  • cli (console messages)
  • taxize (Tropicos API - already in add_entry_taxa())
  • Optional: visNetwork or collapsibleTree (hierarchy visualization)

External APIs

  • Tropicos API: Requires API key (currently TPS_KEY in add_entry_taxa())
    • Store in environment variable or settings
    • Handle API failures gracefully

Error Handling

Common Scenarios

  1. No database connection: Show login panel
  2. Insufficient permissions: Display warning, disable write operations
  3. Duplicate entry: Show existing record, prevent creation
  4. Tropicos API failure: Allow manual entry
  5. Invalid taxonomy: Display validation errors inline
  6. Network issues: Graceful degradation, retry options

User Feedback

  • Success: Green notification (5 sec)
  • Warning: Yellow notification (10 sec)
  • Error: Red notification (persistent, manual dismiss)
  • Progress: Loading spinners for long operations
  • Validation: Inline field-level messages

Future Enhancements (Out of Scope for v1)

  1. Bulk operations:
    • Import taxa from CSV
    • Batch synonym updates
    • Merge duplicate entries
  2. Advanced features:
    • Taxon merge (combine two taxa)
    • Split taxon (separate varieties)
    • Taxonomic changes timeline
    • Export subset of backbone
  3. Integration:
    • Link to plot data showing usage
    • Link to trait data
    • Export to Darwin Core format
  4. Collaboration:
    • Suggested changes workflow (non-admin users)
    • Review/approval system
    • Change proposals discussion

Estimated Timeline

  • Phase 1 (Core structure): 1-2 days
  • Phase 2 (Add functionality): 2-3 days
  • Phase 3 (Synonymy management): 2 days
  • Phase 4 (Visualization & polish): 1-2 days
  • Phase 5 (Documentation & testing): 2 days

Total: ~8-11 days

Success Criteria

✅ App successfully connects to taxa database ✅ Users can search and browse taxonomic data ✅ Users can add new taxa (all ranks: class → variety) ✅ Tropicos integration works ✅ Users can update existing taxa ✅ Users can set/cancel synonymy ✅ Synonym cascade handled correctly ✅ All operations logged in modification history ✅ Full French translation ✅ Graceful error handling ✅ Session cleanup prevents connection errors ✅ Backup records created before modifications

Notes

  • This app operates ONLY on taxa database (unlike query_plots which uses main DB)
  • Write operations require special permissions - verify on connect
  • Taxonomic validation is critical - better to be strict than create bad data
  • Modification history is essential for audit trail
  • Consider adding “dry run” mode for testing without writing to DB
